evidence.title: Every claim is walk-back-able.
evidence.subtitle: AI summaries are only useful if you can check them. Click a finding, and QualiPulse shows you the verbatim quote, the participant, and the timestamp it came from. Try it:

claims.title: Cancellation is a billing-moment event
claims.sub: 9 of 12 participants located the decision at a statement, renewal email, or price change, not at a moment of product frustration.
claims.quote: “I wasn’t even annoyed at the product. <m>The renewal email landed and I just thought, that’s €29 I didn’t decide to spend.</m> That was the whole thing.”

claims.title: “Pause” is the unbuilt feature they wanted
claims.sub: Participants didn’t want to leave. They wanted to stop paying during low-usage months without losing history.
claims.quote: “<m>If I could have frozen it for the summer I’d still be a customer.</m> Instead the options were pay or delete, so… I deleted.”

claims.title: Losing history is the real switching cost
claims.sub: Fear of losing past work kept several participants subscribed months after they stopped using the product weekly.
claims.quote: “Honestly the only reason I’m still paying is <m>three years of notes are in there and I don’t trust the export</m>. That’s not loyalty, that’s hostage-keeping.”

evidence.note: This traceability runs through the whole product: tag quotes into your own codebook, annotate themes as confirmed or disputed, and re-run the analysis with your notes folded in. The AI drafts; you stay the researcher.

faq.title: The things people ask before their first study.

items.question: What exactly costs a credit?
items.answer: Only a completed interview of up to 15 minutes. Participants who are screened out, abandon halfway, or hit a technical failure never consume a credit. That risk is ours, not yours.

items.question: Do participants need to install anything?
items.answer: No. They open your link in any browser (phone or laptop), pass a 10-second mic check, and talk. Consent, screening and resume-where-you-left-off are all built into the flow.

items.question: Do I need to recruit participants?
items.answer: QualiPulse gives you shareable links for your own participants: customers, users, a mailing list, an in-product prompt. You stay in control of who you interview.

items.question: Is an AI interviewer as good as a human moderator?
items.answer: For discovery and evaluative research, it’s remarkably close. It never leads the witness, never gets tired on interview #9, and asks follow-ups grounded in what the participant just said. For deeply sensitive topics, we’d still recommend a human. The honest pitch: an AI-moderated interview beats the survey you were going to send instead.

items.question: How do I know the analysis isn’t hallucinated?
items.answer: Every theme, tension and recommendation carries verbatim quotes that link to the exact transcript turn. Click through and read the source. You can mark themes confirmed, disputed or needs-evidence, and the refined analysis has to answer to your annotations.

items.question: What languages are supported?
items.answer: Interviews run in the language of your study. English, French, German, Spanish, Portuguese and Italian are available today, and we add more regularly. The researcher workspace is available in English and French, and any transcript can be machine-translated as a reading aid, with the original always kept as the source of truth.

items.question: Who owns the research data?
items.answer: You do. Recordings, transcripts and reports belong to your workspace, databases live in the EU, audio is encrypted at rest, and we never train AI models on your research. GDPR-aligned processing with a signed DPA, subprocessor list and participant notice available. AI transcription and analysis run through OpenAI and Anthropic under standard contractual clauses, listed on our subprocessors page.

churn.metaTitle: Churn interviews with your cancelled users · QualiPulse
churn.metaDescription: Interview last month's churned users by voice, without scheduling. Get the switching moment, the trigger and what would have kept them, traced to verbatim quotes.
churn.h1: Why are your users churning? Ask them this week.
churn.sub: Your analytics show where people drop. Thirty voice interviews with cancelled accounts show why, and which fix would have kept them.
when: Churn or downgrades are up and the exit survey says "too expensive" with no detail.
A cohort stalls at the same onboarding step and nobody knows what they expected there.
A feature shipped, adoption stayed flat, and the roadmap meeting is next week.

design.participants: 24 to 36 completed interviews across two or three cohorts: churned, at-risk, engaged
design.field: 48 hours of field time, memo on day three
design.deliverable: Top three causes, trigger moments, rescue features, timestamped quotes, one recommendation

questions: Take me back to the week you decided to cancel. What happened?
What were you hoping to accomplish when you signed up?
What would have made you stay?

output.theme: The decision happens at renewal, not during usage.
output.stat: 11 of 16 churned participants only reassessed value when the renewal email landed.
output.quote: I wasn't especially unhappy. <m>The renewal just made me ask whether I still used it enough.</m>

whatYouGet: A ranked list of churn drivers, each backed by named participants.
The exact words customers use, ready for the retention email or the pricing page.
A memo you can forward to the roadmap meeting, with every claim one click from its quote.

messageTesting.metaTitle: Message and concept testing with real buyers · QualiPulse
messageTesting.metaDescription: Test two or three propositions with thirty real buyers before launch. Unaided understanding, objections and the words they use, from voice interviews you run in days.
messageTesting.h1: Launch the message your customers understand, not the one your team prefers.
messageTesting.sub: Put your propositions in front of real buyers before the launch meeting. Learn which one lands, for whom, and in which words.
when: A launch, repositioning or new landing page is two weeks out and the copy is still a debate.
Pricing or packaging is changing and you need to hear how buyers describe the value.
Two taglines split the team and a five-person call will not settle it.

design.participants: 30 to 45 people, 10 to 15 per strategic segment
design.deliverable: Winning message, the words customers use, top objections, segment by proposition heatmap, launch or rework recommendation

questions: In your own words, what does this company do?
Which problem does this solve for you, if any?
What do you use today for this?
Here is a second version. Which one would you rather see on a landing page, and why?

output.theme: "Automation" describes the technology. "No more chasing approvals" describes the benefit.
output.stat: 9 of 12 buyers picked the outcome-led line and repeated it back correctly.
output.quote: "Automate your finance workflow" sounds generic. <m>"Stop chasing five people to close the month" speaks to me straight away.</m>

whatYouGet: A winner, plus why it wins and for which segment.
The objections to answer on the page before they reach sales.
Customer language you can paste into the headline.

nps.metaTitle: NPS and CSAT deep-dive interviews · QualiPulse
nps.metaDescription: Turn NPS and CSAT scores into voice conversations with detractors, passives and promoters. Root causes, moments of truth and a prioritised CX backlog in days.
nps.h1: Your NPS gives you a score. Get the story behind it.
nps.sub: A four-word survey comment is not a root cause. Invite respondents to a twelve-minute conversation and find out what actually happened.
when: NPS or CSAT dropped this quarter and leadership is asking why.
A new complaint theme shows up in tickets and the open comments are too short to act on.
A post-purchase or onboarding touchpoint is underperforming and the fix is not obvious.

design.participants: 36 to 60 respondents, or 15 detractors, 15 passives and 15 promoters
design.field: Invites on day zero, collection over two to four days, root-cause memo by day five
design.deliverable: Driver tree, moments of truth, themes by segment, quotes, prioritised CX backlog

questions: What was going through your mind when you picked that number?
Was there one moment that weighed most on the score?
Walk me through it from the start. What did you expect to happen?
What did it cost you, practically speaking?
If we changed one thing, what would move your score?

output.theme: The problem is not average delivery time. It is the absence of a reliable new date after a first delay.
output.stat: 13 of 15 detractors described a missed update, not a slow delivery.
output.quote: I could live with the delay. <m>What got me was nobody telling me the new date, so I kept checking.</m>

whatYouGet: Root causes tied to a moment in the journey, not to a score band.
Themes split by detractors, passives and promoters.
A backlog ordered by how many people hit the same wall.
